case_title: N Parameswaran Unni v. G Kannan and Another
accused_victim_relationship: Acquaintance (borrower from the complainant, a creditor relationship)
statutory_provisions: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 s.138 read with s.142
evidence_type: Documentary (dishonoured cheques, bank intimation memo, legal notices with postal endorsements)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.138 NI Act; sentenced to three months simple imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Revision allowed; concurrent conviction set aside on ground that second notice was beyond 15 days
offence_finally_established: Dishonour of cheque under Section 138 read with Section 142, Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881
neutral_facts: The accused borrowed Rs. 64,000 from the complainant in October 1990 and issued two cheques dated 13 October 1990, for Rs. 10,000 and Rs. 25,000, drawn on his bank. A third cheque for Rs. 29,000, dated 8 October 1990, was issued by a different drawer and drawn on another bank. The complainant presented the two cheques to his bank on 4 April 1991. The drawee bank returned them on 5 April 1991 with the endorsement 'Refer to drawer.' The complainant's bank sent an intimation memo dated 5 April 1991, received on 8 April 1991. On 12 April 1991 the complainant sent a legal notice demanding payment to the accused. The postal department returned it on 20 April 1991 with the endorsement 'intimation served, addressee absent'; the complainant's advocate received it on 25 April 1991. A second notice was sent on 4 May 1991 and was returned with the endorsement 'Refused, returned to sender.' The accused did not repay the borrowed amount.
financial_property_loss: Cheques for Rs. 10,000 and Rs. 25,000 dishonoured; loan of Rs. 64,000 alleged by complainant as unpaid
motive: alleged: non-repayment of borrowed money (the court did not decide motive)
key_evidence_accepted: First legal notice dated 12-04-1991 sent by registered post to the correct address, deemed served; cheques, bank intimation and postal endorsements
bail_history: Bail granted to the first respondent; to be cancelled if the deposit is not made
trial_duration: offence: not given; trial judgment: 29-07-1993; High Court: 06-10-2003; Supreme Court: March 2017 (per header)
legal_representation: For the complainant/appellant: M. Gireesh Kumar, Sriram P., Ms. Athira G. Nair (for Ankur S. Kulkarni). For the accused/respondent: C. K. Sasi, Manu Krishnan G., Abraham Mathews (for P. V. Dinesh). No State counsel appears as the proceeding is a private complaint.
investigation_status: Private complaint lodged on 23.05.1991; trial completed; no police investigation mentioned
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted, three months simple imprisonment (29-07-1993). Appellate court: appeal dismissed (07-07-1995). High Court: revision allowed, conviction set aside (06-10-2003). Supreme Court: High Court judgment set aside; conviction restored in default of deposit, otherwise payment of Rs. 2,00,000 in lieu of imprisonment.
legal_principle_applied: Notice sent by registered post to the correct address is deemed served (s.27 General Clauses Act, s.114 Evidence Act), rebuttable by drawer; a reminder notice is not an admission of non-service; complaint must be filed within the time under s.142(b)
precedent_relied_upon: M/s New India Sugar Mills Ltd v. Commissioner of Sales Tax, AIR 1963 SC 1207; Jagdish Singh v. Natthu Singh, (1992) 1 SCC 647; State of M.P. v. Hiralal, (1996) 7 SCC 523; V. Raja Kumari v. P. Subbarama Naidu, (2004) 8 SCC 774
other_sentence_order: Deposit Rs. 2,00,000 by 30.04.2017 before JFCM-II Alappuzha in lieu of three months' imprisonment; Rs. 1,30,000 of it to be paid to the complainant as compensation; if not deposited, conviction and sentence restored and bail cancelled
